results.name: Commemorative inkwell
results.description:
he inkwell is made of purple blown glass, coloured with the use of nickel oxide or manganese oxide. It has the shape of a short cuboid with a square base and bevelled corners. The neck of the vessel is short, round and enclosed by an annular fitting of thin gold sheet with an engraved inscription, reading: “May 3, 1791, Count Stanisław Nałęcz Małachowski”.

On the interior walls of the case, two brass plates with engraved inscriptions were attached, which read: “The Constitution of the Third of May | was signed | using the ink from this inkwell” and “It belonged to Marshal | Małachowski, and later to his nephew Onufry | It was taken over by the Tarnowski family | after his and his wife’s, née Tarnowska, death”.

Time and place of creation: late 18th century, Poland

Jagiellonian University Museum Collegium Maius

Inventory number: 6292; 4215/IV

https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/2842

results.name: The Antrim Cross
results.description: Materials: Bronze, Enamel. Accession no: HCA 627. Current Location: [The Hunt Museum](https://www.huntmuseum.com/) [Limerick](https://www.geonames.org/7778675/limerick-city.html). The Antrim Cross is a bronze cross with five equal arms from the [early 9th century](http://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p08m57h8zmq). The cross has five pyramidal bosses each in the form of a truncated pyramid. The side of the pyramids are decorated with interlocking angular fields of yellow enamel, alternating with a similar-coloured design of an arrow within a truncated triangle. The taller central boss and has an animal design. The flat tops are decorated with small squares of [millefiori](http://www.getty.edu/vow/AATFullDisplay?find=millefiori&logic=AND&note=&english=N&prev_page=1&subjectid=300207352) enamel. Rivet-holes in the separately cast base-plate show that this cross was attached another surface. It is the only virtually intact example of its kind and period. [More](https://tinyurl.com/2rjm9wy7).

results.name: Gilded Brooch (NHMW-PRAE-35.645)
results.description:
3D scan of a gilded brooch with Almandine inlays from the Migration Period In the 6th Century.  This brooch from Perchtoldsdorf/Lower Austria is square headed and shows several animal heads on the head plate as well as on the rhombic footplate. It is cast in silver, gilded and decorated with almandine inlays and niello. It was produced in the 6th Century, when Lombard groups inhabited the region.

This brooch is Number 40 of the NHM Top 100 and can be found in the Treasury Cabinet of the NHM Vienna.

**Specimen**:  Migration Period gilded brooch

**Inventory number**: NHMW-PRAE-35.645

**Collection**: Natural History Museum Vienna, Prehistory Dept., Historical Archaeology Coll. (contact: Stefan Eichert) 

Find out more about the NHMW [here](http://www.nhm-wien.ac.at/en).

Scanned and edited by Irina Huller, Daniel Oberndorfer, Viola Winkler & Anna Haider (NHMW)

results.name: Fast Armored Toilet
results.description:
The Fast Armored Skibidi Toilet's toilet bowl resembles a typical toilet found in American prisons, being shaped like a square with the base in the bottom, as well as a small sink at the top of the toilet. He sports a black Helmet on top of his head, securely fastened with a strap. This character has male_05's head with white eyes.

Behind him is a gigantic metal plate with six rockets attached to the back, allowing the toilet to propel himself at great speeds. His eyes are uniquely white in all his appearances. The flusher lever was possibly seen on top of the actual toilet itself, although it is not known whether that was actually the lever.

results.name: Wooden_Tray
results.description:
Wooden_Tray
***목판***
A vessel used to hold or transport rice cakes or fruit. It is also called a seedbed because it is made of square wooden boards. The front is tilted outward by about 45°, and the inside and outside are lacquered. The materials used are mainly jujube trees and birch trees. The shape varies from rectangular, square, octagonal, etc., and the size varies from around 1 to 2 m to around 10 m. Sometimes, there are extravagant ones with wooden plate ears and brass decorations, and sometimes 10 to 12 pieces are stacked together like a multi-story pagoda in a temple. Explanation Source : Encyclopedia of Korean Culture

results.name: Mariensäule
results.description: Marian or plague column in Marz. The column originally stood on the old main square and was moved to Ambrosius Salzer Square when the square in front of the church was redesigned in 1968. It was built after the plague epidemic in 1713 and features a relief depiction of St. Kajetan on the square base. On a cover plate - St. Sebastian on the left and St. Roch on the right - there is a tall Corinthian column in the middle with the figure of the Eisenstadt miraculous image. The foundation inscription is inscribed on the back of the base.

results.name: Pranger
results.description: Pillory from the 17th century on the upper market square of Grafenschlag. On the round pedestal and round base a square base plate, on it an eight-sided granite pillar with square new end. Above this a larger and on it a smaller eight-sided truncated stone pyramid, on it a stone sphere. On the side there is a neck ring with a stone ball and an iron cross. The pillory was destroyed in 1824 and completed and rebuilt in 1894.

results.name: Gerlach repetitive compass theodolite

user.displayName: Museum of Engineering and Technology, Krakow

results.description:
The theodolite is the basic measurement instrument used in land surveying and construction. It allows measuring distances between points in the field based on angles measured and trigonometric calculations performed. The main parts of a theodolite are the base plate (for mounting on a tripod), limbus (circle plate) and the alidade, i.e. the turning part, which includes the scope, among other parts. The presented repetitive (bi-axial) theodolite in the field in reference to geographic directions. The instrument was made in the Fabryka Instrumentów Geodezyjnych Gustawa Gerlacha in Warsaw in 1938 or a little earlier. The establishment operated from 1816 to the World War II, and it specialised in producing land surveying instruments such as the theodolites, levellers, rangefinders, steel squares, and topographic tables. 

Manufacturer: Fabryka Instrumentów Geodezyjnych G. Gerlach, 1938

Inv. No.: MIM1255/XI-107

Model prepared on the basis of photogrammetric measurements.

results.name: Brooch
results.description:
**Collection:** Roman Archeology Dept.
 
**Inv.-No.:** [CAR-M-8263](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1484772)

**Material:** Bronze, enamel 

**Dimensions:** 3,3 x 2,2 cm

**Dating:** 2nd half of the 1st - 1st half of the 2nd century AD

A square plate positioned transversely to the axis of the pin. The plate has a raised, horizontally placed central bar with seven square recesses, which are filled with four blue, two green, and one red enamel inlays, some of which are still preserved. On either side of the bar, there is a wavy band framed by two notched strips. Along the longitudinal axis, there are profiled extensions. The hinge construction and the catchplate are preserved, but the pin is missing.

This object was digitized through the 'Kulturerbe digital' program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

results.name: Pranger
results.description:
In 1804, the pillory was erected in front of the building; until then, it had been located in front of the stately inn on the Platzl (today's main square). The pillory column dates back to the 17th century. Today, the pillory stands next to the Pinkafeld Town and Clothmakers' Museum.

The pillory consists of a square stone pillar on a pedestal. On the top plate is a stone urn bearing the date 1804. A piece of chain with a ball hangs from the side. Double handcuffs are attached to the front, as well as a recess with a hole for inserting a so-called court arm. This wooden, painted arm with a sword was considered a symbol of the Ius gladii (term for the legal authority to pronounce and execute the death penalty outside Rome within the framework of capital jurisdiction).

In the past, the arm was only attached during court proceedings. Today, a replica is permanently mounted on the pillory.

results.name: Anchor brooch
results.description:
**Collection:** Roman Archeology Dept.
 
**Inv.-No.:** [CAR-M-6441](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1474415)

**Material:** Bronze 

**Dimensions:** 5,3 x 3,3 cm

**Dating:** 2nd-3rd century AD 

The wide headpiece of the bracket features a broadly curved protrusion (anchor) on both sides, ending in a button. At the top of the bow, there is a triple button. Another solid button is located at the foot end. The spring with 13 coils is covered by a narrow, stepped, square spring plate. Between the spring plate and the headpiece, there are crescent-shaped notches. The catchplate is perforated. The pin is preserved.

This object was digitized through the 'Kulturerbe digital' program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

results.name: Executioner's stone (Lublin legend)
results.description:
**This stone was used as a base for the executioner's stump on Bernardyński Square, where an unfortunate accident occurred. Later, it was moved to Rybna Street, where the scent of spilled soup attracted nearby dogs that died after licking the stone. People became convinced that touching the stone brings bad luck. The stone was also used to build an oven in a bakery, which ended in tragedy. Finally, it ended up on Litewski Square, where a soldier fell on it and lost his life. The stone still lies near the Trynitarska Tower, showing a notch from the executioner's sword.**

**Photogrammetric scan (50 x 12MP 4:3); captured 27 Feb 2023, converted to low-poly quad mesh (2.4k faces); processed in Metashape, editing done in blender, remeshed via QuadRemesher, includes:**

* 4k    80%JPG   diffuse 
* 4k    80%JPG   normal
* 2k    80%JPG   metalic
* 2k    80%JPG   ambient occlusion
* 2k    80%JPG   roughness

Size: ~ 0.7 x 0.7 x 0.3 meters

Memorial located in Lublin, Poland (https://osm.org/go/0kBUpGgTx?m=)
